Finding and downloading PRIDE Archive data

Source: vignettes/pride.Rmd
pride.Rmd

The pride_ functions find PRIDE Archive projects, list their files and download the ones you choose, using mzLib’s paging and URL resolution.

question function mzLib
which projects are about my subject? pride_search() PrideArchiveClient.SearchProjectsAsync
what files does a project have, with categories and checksums? pride_list_files() PrideArchiveClient.GetProjectFilesAsync
every file, including ones the manifest omits pride_list_ftp_files() PrideArchiveClient.GetProjectFilesFromFtpAsync
how big is it, before I download? pride_approximate_total_size_bytes(), pride_total_size_bytes() PrideArchiveExtensions.TotalApproximateSizeBytes
download the files I picked pride_download_files() PrideArchiveClient.DownloadFileAsync
download by category or extension pride_download() PrideArchiveClient.DownloadProjectFilesAsync
is my download the file PRIDE holds? pride_file_checksums() PrideArchiveClient.GetFileChecksumsAsync

Find a project

pride_search() is the discovery step: it turns a subject into the accessions every other function takes, with every page fetched and no accession repeated.

hits <- pride_search("plasmodium falciparum schizont")
hits[, c("accession", "submission_type", "publication_date")]
#>   accession submission_type publication_date
#> 1 PXD070842        COMPLETE       2026-06-01
#> 2 PXD020210        COMPLETE       2021-01-25
#> 3 PXD020189        COMPLETE       2021-01-25
#> 4 PXD008250         PARTIAL       2018-02-13
#> 5 PXD001684         PARTIAL       2015-04-23
#> 6 PXD000070        COMPLETE       2014-04-24
hits$organisms[[1]]
#> [1] "Homo sapiens (human)"                "Plasmodium falciparum (isolate 3d7)"
hits$matched_fields[[1]]
#> [1] "references" "title"

A hit is a search-index projection, not the project’s metadata: vocabulary fields arrive as display strings with no accessions, a count of 0 means “not reported”, and project_file_names is not the manifest. Follow the accession.

List, then choose with [ 

files <- pride_list_files("PXD000001")
files[, c("file_name", "category", "size_mb", "downloadable")]
#>                                                     file_name category
#> 1                  PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mztab.gz    OTHER
#> 2                    PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mgf.gz     PEAK
#> 3 TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.mzXML     PEAK
#> 4                                    erwinia_carotovora.fasta    OTHER
#> 5   TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.raw      RAW
#> 6                                       F063721.dat-mztab.txt    OTHER
#> 7                          PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.xml.gz   RESULT
#> 8                                                 F063721.dat   SEARCH
#>      size_mb downloadable
#> 1   0.497985         TRUE
#> 2  16.448103         TRUE
#> 3 243.031280         TRUE
#> 4   1.657668         TRUE
#> 5 220.475548         TRUE
#> 6   0.304798         TRUE
#> 7  10.677205         TRUE
#> 8  21.185462         TRUE

Choose rows with ordinary subsetting, then pass them to pride_download_files(). That says things the category and extensions filters of pride_download() cannot, such as “under 5 MB” or “everything except the raw file”.

small <- files[files$size_mb < 5 & files$downloadable, ]
small$file_name
#> [1] "PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mztab.gz"
#> [2] "erwinia_carotovora.fasta"                  
#> [3] "F063721.dat-mztab.txt"
pride_total_size_bytes(small)
#> [1] 2460451
# Not run: downloads from PRIDE.
pride_download_files(small, "downloads")

Two things the manifest will not tell you

Sizes can be the decompressed size. For some compressed files PRIDE reports the size of the content, not of the download: the .mgf.gz above is listed at 16 MB and transfers 6 MB. Treat pride_total_size_bytes() as an upper bound.

The manifest can be incomplete. PRIDE’s REST API omits some of PXD000001’s files, including the two largest. pride_list_ftp_files() walks the project’s FTP tree instead, subdirectories included:

listing <- pride_list_ftp_files("PXD000001")
c(ftp_tree = nrow(listing), rest_manifest = nrow(files))
#>      ftp_tree rest_manifest 
#>            14             8
listing[, c("relative_path", "approximate_size_mb")]
#>                                                           relative_path
#> 1                                                           F063721.dat
#> 2                                                 F063721.dat-mztab.txt
#> 3                                    PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.xml.gz
#> 4                                      PRIDE_Exp_mzData_Ac_22134.xml.gz
#> 5                                PXD000001_community_annotated.sdrf.tsv
#> 6                                                   PXD000001_mztab.txt
#> 7                                                            README.txt
#> 8   TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01-20141210.mzML
#> 9  TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01-20141210.mzXML
#> 10          TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.mzXML
#> 11            TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.raw
#> 12                                             erwinia_carotovora.fasta
#> 13                   generated/PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mgf.gz
#> 14                 generated/PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mztab.gz
#>    approximate_size_mb
#> 1            20.971520
#> 2             0.305152
#> 3            10.485760
#> 4             9.751757
#> 5             0.004096
#> 6             0.864256
#> 7             0.001638
#> 8           449.839104
#> 9           472.907776
#> 10          243.269632
#> 11          220.200960
#> 12            1.677722
#> 13            5.976883
#> 14            0.103424
round(pride_approximate_total_size_bytes(listing) / 1e9, 2)   # GB
#> [1] 1.44

A file that appears only there is fetched from its url with any HTTPS client, for example download.file().

Filters that match nothing are errors

pride_download() with a category or extensions filter that matches nothing raises, rather than reporting success with nothing downloaded. A compressed file’s extension is .gz, so extensions = ".mgf" matches nothing in PXD000001:

# Not run: downloads from PRIDE.
pride_download("PXD000001", "downloads", category = "PEAK", extensions = ".gz")

An unknown accession raises mzlib_project_not_found rather than returning nothing:

tryCatch(pride_list_files("PXD999999999"),
         mzlib_project_not_found = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
#> [1] "PRIDE returned no files for 'PXD999999999'. Either the accession does not exist (check for a typo) or the project is private. PRIDE does not distinguish the two, so neither can mzLibR."

An EBI outage raises mzlib_service_unavailable. See ?mzlib_error, and the next section for what to do about one.

Retries, timeouts and outages

mzLib retries for you. A PRIDE request that fails in a way that can pass (no answer, an HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx, or a 403 from EBI’s FTP host, its rate limit) is retried three times, after 5, 20 and 60 seconds, and that request alone (mzLib #1412). A paged manifest retries only the page that failed, and a download resumes where it stopped.

mzLibR adds no timeout of its own by default, on any pride_ function. Each attempt is already limited to 100 seconds, so an outage that hangs is reported as mzlib_service_unavailable after about 8 minutes per request. Pass timeout to cut a call off sooner; it then raises mzlib_timeout, which is not mzlib_service_unavailable:

# Not run: contacts PRIDE.
pride_list_files("PXD000001", timeout = 60)   # give up after a minute

By the time mzlib_service_unavailable reaches you, mzLib has already retried, so retrying again at once rarely helps. Wait minutes, not seconds:

# Not run: shows how to handle a PRIDE outage, which a recording cannot produce.
files <- tryCatch(
  pride_list_files("PXD000001"),
  mzlib_service_unavailable = function(e) {
    Sys.sleep(600)   # mzLib retried already; give EBI ten minutes
    pride_list_files("PXD000001")
  }
)

Two failures look like a request PRIDE refused, mzlib_bridge_error with error_type "HttpRequestException", but are EBI’s: an FTP listing that came back empty, and a 403 from EBI’s FTP host, each still failing after mzLib’s retries. Treat those as an outage.

Interrupted and suspect downloads

Each file streams to a temporary .partial name and moves into place only once complete, so a cancelled or crashed download leaves no truncated file under its real name. A transfer that fails after mzLib’s retries leaves <name>.partial and <name>.partial.validator in the folder on purpose: the next call for that file resumes from them (mzLib #1412). Leave them in place, or delete both to start over.

mzLib can check a download against PRIDE’s checksums, and catch an EBI error page served at the right size (mzLib #1427, #1449). That check is not yet on the path pride_download() and pride_download_files() use, so a file can be reported as downloaded when its bytes are wrong. For files that matter, check each one against pride_file_checksums() before you search it, as the next section shows.

Checking a download against PRIDE’s checksums

Is the file on your disk the file PRIDE holds? The download functions cannot tell you yet. PRIDE records an MD5 and the exact size of every file a submitter deposits, and pride_file_checksums() returns that record. Its row names are the file names, so look a file up by the name it was downloaded under:

checksums <- pride_file_checksums("PXD000001")
nrow(checksums)
#> [1] 12
checksums["TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.raw", c("md5", "size_bytes")]
#>                                                                                        md5
#> TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.raw c567cecbb9866796e690a4958746f7b6
#>                                                           size_bytes
#> TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.raw  220475548

md5 is 32 hexadecimal characters, as PRIDE wrote them; compare it without regard to case. size_bytes is the exact length a download of the file comes to, which neither other listing gives you. pride_list_ftp_files() rounds its sizes, and pride_list_files() can be wrong:

gz <- "PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.xml.gz"
c(manifest = files$file_size_bytes[files$file_name == gz], checksums = checksums[gz, "size_bytes"])
#>  manifest checksums 
#>  10677205  10668000

The download is 10,668,000 bytes, the checksum list’s number. Because each size is exact, so is their sum: what the deposited files weigh, without the generated/ files, which have no row (below).

round(sum(checksums$size_bytes) / 1e9, 2)   # GB
#> [1] 1.43

The check

A file is PRIDE’s when its length and its MD5 both match. The length costs nothing to check. The MD5 reads the whole file, a few seconds per gigabyte. Check both, because the length alone does not prove the bytes: on 7 and 8 October 2026, EBI served about 23 of about 70 large transfers at the right size with its own error text written over part of them (mzLib #1449). Base R has all it takes:

check_download <- function(path, expected) {
  # NA when the file is the one PRIDE recorded, otherwise what is wrong with it.
  size <- file.size(path)
  if (size != expected$size_bytes) {
    return(paste(size, "bytes where PRIDE records", expected$size_bytes))
  }
  md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(path))
  if (md5 != tolower(expected$md5)) {
    return(paste("MD5", md5, "where PRIDE records", expected$md5))
  }
  NA_character_
}

Here it is on two damaged copies of the project’s 1,645-byte README.txt. The first was cut short. The second is the right size with EBI’s error text inside, and only the MD5 catches it:

readme <- checksums["README.txt", ]
damaged <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeBin(charToRaw(strrep("x", 1000)), damaged)
check_download(damaged, readme)
#> [1] "1000 bytes where PRIDE records 1645"
error_page <- "<Error><Code>ConnectionClosedException</Code></Error>"
writeBin(charToRaw(paste0(error_page, strrep(".", 1645 - nchar(error_page)))), damaged)
check_download(damaged, readme)
#> [1] "MD5 6a8f1a7d39089d34bf9bc9b19e553dd4 where PRIDE records 492753137013825025e6729c8798664f"

After a real download, check every file it wrote:

# Not run: downloads files from PRIDE.
paths <- pride_download("PXD000001", "downloads", category = "RAW")
checksums <- pride_file_checksums("PXD000001")
for (path in paths) {
  name <- basename(path)
  if (!name %in% rownames(checksums)) {
    message(name, ": PRIDE has no checksum for it, so it cannot be checked")
    next
  }
  problem <- check_download(path, checksums[name, ])
  if (!is.na(problem)) message(name, ": ", problem, ". Download it again.")
}

To download a damaged file again, pass its row to pride_download_files(), or call pride_download() with overwrite = TRUE, the default. overwrite = FALSE would skip it, because it is already there.

What the list covers

It covers the files the submitter deposited at the project’s root. It is a third list, not a view of either of the others, and three things follow from that.

PRIDE’s own generated/ files have no row. A file without a row cannot be checked; that does not make it invalid. In PXD000001 those are the two files under generated/, which pride_list_files() names without their folder:

listing$relative_path[!listing$relative_path %in% checksums$file_name]
#> [1] "generated/PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mgf.gz"  
#> [2] "generated/PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mztab.gz"
files$file_name[!files$file_name %in% checksums$file_name]
#> [1] "PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mztab.gz"
#> [2] "PRIDE_Exp_Complete_Ac_22134.pride.mgf.gz"

It names files the REST manifest omits, such as the 450 MB .mzML that only the FTP listing showed above:

"TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01-20141210.mzML" %in% checksums$file_name
#> [1] TRUE

It can name files that are not deposits at all. PXD015239’s list includes a 2.3 GB NFS temp file, .nfs80360b91005fae5300002478. Look up the files you have by name; do not read the list as the project’s contents.

Two traps

The manifest’s checksum column is not this MD5. Where PRIDE fills it in, it is a 40-character SHA-1, a different digest of the same bytes. For every PXD000001 file it is empty:

unique(files$checksum)
#> [1] ""

Zero rows is an answer. It means the project exists but PRIDE holds no checksums for it, so nothing can be checked. An accession PRIDE does not know raises mzlib_project_not_found, and so does a project not yet published: PRIDE holds no checksums before publication. A list mzLib cannot read (a new header, a malformed row, a name listed twice) is an mzlib_bridge_error with error_type "MzLibException": not your bug, and mzLib does not retry it, so report it.
